_comment: Shape of the --config file for scripts/run-e2e-evidence.mjs. Every path is an absolute local path on the owner's machine, so a real canary configuration is never committed: it would put a private project root into the public repository. Copy this file outside the repository, fill the placeholders and keep the result next to the run it produced, so the run identifiers in the release evidence stay resolvable. The two entries below are independent examples of the same shape, not one configuration: a canary normally names a single project.
output_root: <absolute path to an empty directory; the runner refuses to reuse one>
gateway_entry: <absolute path to AgentGateway/src/cli.mjs of the installation under test>

projects.name: Example web application canary
projects.root_path: <absolute path to the real repository this canary runs against>
projects.message: Run the registered read-only technical verification scenario. Do not edit source files and do not make owner acceptance decisions.

projects.name: Example 1C development canary
projects.root_path: <absolute path to the exported 1C configuration sources this canary runs against>

resources.purpose: Read-only access to the owner's file information base

one_c_bsl._comment: Present only when the canary must prove the BSL gate. The package ships this check disabled because the analyzer is a local binary and the accepted debt is the owner signature, so the canary registers the baseline and binds the analyzer before the run.
one_c_bsl.executable: <absolute path to the local BSL Language Server executable>
one_c_bsl.source: <absolute path to the exported configuration sources; must be a clean git worktree at accepted_revision>
one_c_bsl.platform_bin: <absolute path to the 1C platform bin directory containing shcntx_*.hbk>
one_c_bsl.temp_root: <absolute path to a directory the analyzer may use for scratch files>
one_c_bsl.accepted_revision: <git revision of source whose diagnostics the owner accepts as the baseline>
one_c_bsl.confirmed_by: <the owner who accepts that debt; never defaulted, never synthesized>
